findings.reason: The original standalone 1200x1400 screenshot has no illustration. A two-row local refinement interval with a separate quotient isomorphism materially clarifies the switch from the A-row ordering (i,j) to the B-row ordering (j,i), rather than merely decorating a complete proof.
findings.action: Added a final Remarks illustration of both interval chains and their butterfly quotient pairing, with explicit indexing, arrow meaning, endpoint and zero-factor explanations.

correction: Appended final Remarks only; the entire original item remains an exact byte prefix. Added one TikZ illustration with six subobject-inclusion arrows and one canonical quotient-isomorphism arrow.

diagram_math_checks.data: For 0 <= i < m, 0 <= j < n, the top row is A_i -> A_{i,j} -> A_{i,j+1} -> A_{i+1}.
diagram_math_checks.justification: Step 1.1 defines A_{i,j}=A_i join (A_{i+1} meet B_j). Join includes A_i; monotonicity of B_j <= B_{j+1} gives the middle inclusion; both joined subobjects lie in A_{i+1}, giving the final inclusion. All objects are subobjects of X and arrows represent their monomorphism comparison maps.

diagram_math_checks.data: The second row is B_j -> B_{j,i} -> B_{j,i+1} -> B_{j+1}.
diagram_math_checks.justification: The symmetric definition in step 1.1 gives B_{j,i}=B_j join (B_{j+1} meet A_i). The same monotonicity with A_i <= A_{i+1} proves all three inclusions. These are not vertical comparison maps between the A and B flags.

diagram_math_checks.data: The bottom arrow has domain A_{i,j+1}/A_{i,j} and codomain B_{j,i+1}/B_{j,i}, and is an isomorphism.
diagram_math_checks.justification: Substitute A_0=A_i, A_1=A_{i+1}, B_0=B_j, B_1=B_{j+1} into the local butterfly supplier statement. Its left quotient is the displayed A-factor; commutativity of join identifies its right quotient with the displayed B-factor. This is exactly step 2.1. No square, extra commutativity, exactness or stronger categorical hypothesis is asserted.

diagram_math_checks.data: Intervals concatenate and repeated terms remove matched zero factors.
diagram_math_checks.justification: B_0=0 and B_n=X give A_{i,0}=A_i and A_{i,n}=A_{i+1}; symmetrically A_0=0 and A_m=X give the B endpoints. A quotient by the same subobject is zero, and the bottom isomorphism pairs zero with zero, as in steps 1.1 and 3.1. No simplicity, strictness, finite length or elementwise interpretation is assumed.
